text:
Could Week 10 change the fantasy football picture for the rest of the season? With the 2026 NFL campaign reaching its halfway point, injuries to several big names could force managers to rethink their lineups. Patrick Mahomes, Puka Nacua, Josh Jacobs and Rhamondre Stevenson headline the latest injury concerns.

Four teams are also on a bye, while quarterback injuries in Seattle and Arizona could open the door for backup players. Here’s a closer look at the major NFL injuries ahead of Week 10.

ADVERTISEMENT

Quarterbacks

Quarterback injuries could become one of the biggest talking points ahead of Week 10. Several teams are dealing with uncertainty at the position.

Patrick Mahomes (Chiefs, elbow): Mahomes injured his elbow during the Week 9 game against the Jets. However, he returned to the field and helped Kansas City secure a 35-12 victory. He completed 23 of 31 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns.

ADVERTISEMENT

Head coach Andy Reid said Mahomes is day-to-day after an MRI showed no major damage. He could play against the Falcons, but Justin Fields is expected to start if Mahomes cannot recover in time. His absence would also affect Rashee Rice and Travis Kelce.

ADVERTISEMENT

Sam Darnold and Drew Lock (Seahawks): Darnold will miss the Week 10 game against the Raiders because of quad and rib injuries. Lock is expected to start after medical tests on his oblique injury showed positive results. The Raiders have allowed the fifth-most fantasy points to quarterbacks this season. This makes Lock an interesting option for fantasy managers.

JJ McCarthy (Giants, hip): McCarthy suffered a hip injury against Philadelphia but is expected to play against Washington on Thursday night. Head coach John Harbaugh suggested that the quarterback should be available. Jameis Winston remains the backup option if McCarthy cannot start.

ADVERTISEMENT

Gardner Minshew (Cardinals, elbow): Minshew is feared to have suffered a torn UCL during Arizona’s Week 9 loss to Seattle. He could miss the rest of the season. If that happens, rookie Carson Beck could take over as the starter. Beck’s arrival could create more opportunities for tight end Trey McBride. However, Arizona’s limited receiving options make the rookie a risky fantasy choice.

Other updates include Kyler Murray, who remains week-to-week with a hamstring injury. Justin Herbert is dealing with a finger problem, while Deshaun Watson is recovering from a concussion. Malik Willis has moved to injured reserve and will miss at least four games. Drew Lock’s expected return as Seattle’s starting quarterback is also an important development for the team’s offense.

ADVERTISEMENT

Running Backs

Several running backs are dealing with injuries ahead of Week 10. Their availability could also create new opportunities for backup players.

ADVERTISEMENT

Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson (Patriots): New England could face a major problem in its backfield against Detroit in Germany. Stevenson left the Week 9 loss to Green Bay with a knee injury. Reports suggest that a tendon problem could keep him out for a short period.

Henderson has also missed time after experiencing unexplained neurological symptoms. He was ruled out again because of an illness. If both players remain unavailable, Corey Kiner could become New England’s lead running back. He finished Week 9 with 55 rushing yards and one touchdown on eight carries.

Josh Jacobs (Packers, finger): Jacobs fractured a finger against New England and could miss up to three or four weeks. He may remain out until at least Week 13. Kaleb Johnson could become one of his replacements after recording 68 rushing yards and a touchdown on 14 carries. Pierre Strong Jr. could also get more chances, while MarShawn Lloyd is another player to watch. Johnson is worth considering on fantasy waiver wires, although Green Bay faces a difficult matchup against Minnesota.

ADVERTISEMENT

Cam Skattebo (Giants, hamstring): Skattebo is expected to return after missing Week 9. His return should improve New York’s running game, which struggled without him against Philadelphia.

Other running back updates include Kyle Monangai, who remains a concern for Chicago, although the Bears have a bye in Week 10. Saquon Barkley continues to play through back and hamstring problems. Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon could get more opportunities following Malik Willis’ move to injured reserve. Meanwhile, Jonah Coleman is expected to lead Denver’s backfield with RJ Harvey sidelined.

Wide Receivers

The wide receiver position has also suffered several major injuries. The Rams and Cardinals are among the teams facing the biggest problems.

ADVERTISEMENT

Puka Nacua (Rams, knee/turf toe): Nacua suffered knee sprains and a turf toe injury during the Rams’ Week 9 win over Washington. Head coach Sean McVay suggested that the receiver will likely move to injured reserve. This would be a major setback for Los Angeles, which is already without Davante Adams.

Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell could get more opportunities alongside tight ends Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson, and Davis Allen. The Rams could also depend more on running backs Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. Nacua’s absence would hurt Matthew Stafford’s fantasy value while giving other offensive players a chance to handle bigger roles.

Michael Wilson (Cardinals, neck): Wilson will miss the rest of the 2026 season because of a neck injury. Arizona was already dealing with injuries to several receivers, and his absence creates another problem. Rookie Carson Beck could take over at quarterback, while Trey McBride is likely to play an even bigger role in the passing game. Simi Fehoko, Reggie Virgil and Devin Duvernay could also receive more opportunities.

ADVERTISEMENT

George Pickens (Cowboys, hamstring): Pickens missed Dallas’ Week 9 win over Indianapolis. His availability against San Francisco will be important for the Cowboys. CeeDee Lamb recorded 195 receiving yards and one touchdown on 10 catches without Pickens. If Pickens misses another game, Lamb could again receive a large share of the targets. Ryan Flournoy could also become a FLEX option for fantasy managers.

Other wide receiver updates: Ladd McConkey is dealing with back spasms but has extra time to prepare for the Chargers’ Monday night game against Baltimore. Deebo Samuel hopes to return from a hamstring injury, while Mike Evans continues to deal with an Achilles problem. Xavier Worthy is managing a hamstring injury, and Garrett Wilson is recovering from a concussion. A.J. Brown’s knee injury remains a concern, although he is expected to travel to Germany for Week 10.

Luther Burden III and Jaylen Waddle will also get extra time to recover during their teams’ bye weeks.

Tight Ends

Jake Ferguson (Cowboys, knee): Ferguson is expected to miss multiple weeks after suffering a knee injury. Brevin Span-Ford could take over as Dallas’ main tight end during his absence. However, he is not a reliable fantasy option outside deeper leagues.

ADVERTISEMENT

David Njoku is another player to watch. The Chargers are reportedly preparing to open his 21-day practice window. This could bring him closer to a return.

Players out for the season and on IR

Several important players are already expected to miss a long period or the entire 2026 season.

ADVERTISEMENT

Here are some of the biggest names:

Quarterbacks: Jaxson Dart, Jalen Hurts, Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley.

Running backs: Jeremiyah Love, James Conner, RJ Harvey, Tyrone Tracy Jr., Jacory Croskey-Merritt, Jonathon Brooks, Travis Etienne Jr., Will Shipley, Tank Bigsby and Dameon Pierce.

Wide receivers: Ricky Pearsall, Jayden Higgins, Michael Wilson, Terry McLaurin, Jaylin Noel, Davante Adams, Romeo Doubs, Jalen McMillan, De’Zhaun Stribling, Michael Pittman Jr., Roman Wilson and Alec Pierce.

Tight ends: Terrance Ferguson and David Njoku.

These injuries have forced several teams to change their offensive plans. They have also created opportunities for younger players to step into bigger roles.

What to watch before Week 10 kickoff

Patrick Mahomes’ elbow, the Patriots’ running back injuries, J.J. McCarthy’s hip, and George Pickens’ hamstring are some of the biggest concerns heading into Week 10. Puka Nacua and Gardner Minshew could also miss extended time, creating problems for their teams.

Fantasy managers should follow practice reports and injury updates before setting their lineups. A player’s return or absence could create new opportunities for others and change fantasy plans.

title: 10 biggest injuries that have shaped the 2026 NFL season - Yahoo Sports
description:
It has been a tough half season for injuries in the NFL.
Sam Darnold suffered an injury on the first series of the season and missed time in two different stretches for two different injuries.
Let's take a look at the most damaging ones that have helped shape the story of this NFL season's first half.
The Eagles started the season 2-0 but now have lost seven straight, the past four with Hurts out of the lineup.
This is disastrous for a Rams team that put itself in a 2-4 hole to start the season and only recently improved to 5-4.
text:
It has been a tough half season for injuries in the NFL.

It's sometimes difficult to rate just how injurious it has been, relative to other seasons, but there are some clear indications of it. Through Week 9 of the 2025 season, there were 171 players on injured reserve. That number, through Week 9 of this season, is a whopping 280 — a nearly 64% increase.

Of course, that doesn't tell us who is on IR, how serious the injuries are or how many later came off the list. But even casual NFL observers know how hard the quarterback position has been hit.

There are currently five projected starting quarterbacks on injured reserve, including a former MVP (whose backup is also on IR) and a former Super Bowl MVP. Sam Darnold suffered an injury on the first series of the season and missed time in two different stretches for two different injuries.

Amid this carnage, some injuries have hurt more than others. Let's take a look at the most damaging ones that have helped shape the story of this NFL season's first half.

Jalen Hurts, QB, Eagles

Hurts' diagnosis of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in his calf and bilateral pulmonary emboli (blood clots in both lungs) landed him on injured reserve. Without question, this was a massive development that raised questions about Hurts' football future and, even if he's eventually cleared to play again, his future in Philadelphia.

The Eagles have been stockpiling draft picks for the 2027 and 2028 draft cycles, and it's hard not to think that the uncertainty of their former Super Bowl MVP is at least part of that thinking, especially since the team made two notable trades — A.J. Brown and Cam Jurgens — before Hurts' diagnosis.

Hurts' play had leveled off over the past year-plus, but his replacements have fared far worse in his place. The Eagles started the season 2-0 but now have lost seven straight, the past four with Hurts out of the lineup.

Lamar Jackson, QB, Ravens

First, Jackson suffered a high-ankle sprain, knocking him out of the lineup for three games. In that span, the Ravens went from 3-1 to last place in the AFC North. Then, on his first snap back in the lineup, Jackson suffered a broken thumb against the Bills and could be lost for the season.

Jackson reportedly has told teammates he plans to return before the end of the season, which offers a glimmer of hope. But getting him back by Week 16 is optimistic, and the Ravens could be well out of the division race. The injury also compelled the team to trade for Jacoby Brissett in a deal that included a pick swap.

Jackson's future with the Ravens also remains murky. The injuries have started to add up, and after a spring and summer of failed negotiations over a contract extension, it's unclear if either side's thinking has changed about a long-term future in Baltimore.

This injury could have a lasting effect on the relationship between Jackson and the Ravens, but it still would be a surprise if the team sought to trade him in the offseason.

Jaxson Dart, QB, Giants

In Week 2, Dart suffered a knee injury that included a torn meniscus and additional ligament damage. It was seemingly a major setback for a developing team. The good news is that with a 4-6 month recovery timetable, Dart should be ready for at least part of the offseason program, if not all of it.

The injury prompted the Giants to trade for J.J. McCarthy, which has changed the situation in a fascinating way. McCarthy has played better than he did in Minnesota in a small sample size and has at least prompted a conversation about how the Giants will handle the situation next season.

Dart likely remains the team's quarterback, and having McCarthy can be viewed as a "good problem." But it also could fuel some competition there, depending on how McCarthy plays down the stretch and how Dart's rehab progresses.

De'Von Achane, RB, Dolphins

It might be easy to dismiss a very good player such as Achane on a bad team. But we are talking about someone who in 2025 led the NFL in yards per carry and was sixth in all-purpose yards.

The Dolphins rebuffed offseason trade interest in Achane and planned to make him one of their offensive centerpieces. With a first-year head coach and new staff, a new starting quarterback in Malik Willis (with six starts coming into the season) and an extremely young set of receivers, Achane's value to the Dolphins was immense.

And who knows? Had Achane thrived this season rather than tearing his ACL in Week 3, it's possible that Miami could have changed its tune and put Achane up on the trade block. The Dolphins were never expected to be contenders, but his injury has significantly upped the team's degree of difficulty.

Laremy Tunsil, OT, Commanders

We had multiple Commanders injuries from which to choose, including Jayden Daniels missing multiple games, Terry McLaurin being out for the season, or Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw going down before Washington could even consider trading them.

But let's go with Tunsil, whose injury seemed to foretell the Commanders' compounding issues this season. He suffered torn triceps in training camp, underwent surgery and was placed on IR. Though a late-season return is possible, it feels unlikely.

When Tunsil went down, it seemed to have a cumulative effect on the rest of the team. The blocking wasn't as good. Daniels got hurt. Then McLaurin, and so on. It has been a rough season again in Washington, and the Tunsil injury was an early harbinger of things.

Davante Adams and Puka Nacua, WRs, Rams

Adams suffered a significant hamstring injury in Week 6, and the Rams' timeline has him returning as soon as early December or as late as Week 16. Then Nacua went down on the final offensive snap of Sunday's game, and he's expected miss significant time with a right knee injury and turf toe.

This is disastrous for a Rams team that put itself in a 2-4 hole to start the season and only recently improved to 5-4. How will Matthew Stafford fare for the next month without both? (The Rams also have wideout Jordan Whittington on IR.)

They're currently down to Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels and Xavier Smith at wideout. Even with some quality running backs and tight ends on the roster, it might significantly limit what Sean McVay's offense can achieve while battling the 49ers and Seahawks in a stacked NFC West.

Myles Garrett, Edge, Rams

The Rams also suffered on the defensive side. Garrett played in the season opener, but it was clear something was wrong and he underwent arthroscopic knee surgery and was placed on IR. He missed seven games before being activated, and Garrett's impact was immediately clear in his three-sack game Sunday against Washington.

Getting Garrett back to play alongside Aaron Donald could bear some real fruit, but did the earlier damage from his absence — along with the other injuries the Rams have suffered — hurt the Rams enough to prevent them from making a realistic playoff push?

Garrett was the clear-cut top acquisition of the offseason in a blockbuster trade. There was talk of the Rams going 17-0. All that has faded now, even with Garrett's return. We'll have to see if he and others can carry this wounded team down the stretch, but it's a massive ask.

Brian Burns, Edge, Giants

Burns suffering a season-ending ACL injury was a huge setback for a Giants team that could end up taking the NFC East. In addition, the Giants lost linebacker Tremaine Edmunds (torn chest muscle) to a season-ending injury.

Thankfully for the Giants, Abdul Carter has helped create strong pressure in Burns' absence, and Arvell Reese has emerged as a Defensive Rookie of the Year candidate. But when it comes to the Giants being actual contenders, and not just a team taking advantage of a weaker division, Burns' loss is massive.

We can't discount what the Giants have done in the face of major adversity this season. But it's hard to consider them true threats once the playoffs arrive, and Burns' absence is a big reason why.

Edgerrin Cooper, LB, Packers

There's a little liberty with this selection in that, yes, it was a big individual blow for Cooper (season-ending torn Achilles), but it also was one of several defensive injuries that hampered Green Bay this season. The cumulative effect cannot be ignored.

The Packers were already without Micah Parsons, their most impactful defender, as he rehabbed from last year's ACL tear. And he's only recently returned to practice, nearly 11 months after suffering the injury. Then Cooper went down on Oct. 4, followed by defensive tackle Javon Hargrave, who suffered a torn Achilles the following week.

Cooper is a young, high-upside defender who was starting to become a force for the Packers. Parsons is still the defensive centerpiece, and his return could have a huge effect on Green Bay, which has played some inspired ball the past month-plus. But not having Cooper could keep a lid on what this defense's potential might be in the long run.

Chiefs get great news on Patrick Mahomes for Week 10 after major injury scare originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

During the Kansas City Chiefs' Week 9 win over the New York Jets, Patrick Mahomes sustained what initially looked like a significant arm injury.

His right arm was hit hard on a sack by rookie edge rusher David Bailey, and it was easy to fear for the worst, considering how things looked. He came back into the game, which was a sigh of relief, but afterwards there was some real concern.

Fortunately, the initial tests weren't bad, and now on Wednesday, Andy Reid told reporters, including Charles Goldman from A to Z Sports, that Mahomes is expected to be a full participant in practice, pointing to his injury not being a big deal.

Chiefs get huge sigh of relief with Patrick Mahomes after injury scare

"Chiefs HC Andy Reid anticipates full participation from QB Patrick Mahomes (elbow). Says he's throwing the ball well," Goldman reports.

This is a huge piece of news to come out of Reid's press conference. After a major injury scare, the Chiefs have seemingly dodged a bullet with Mahomes' injury.

Based on the fact that he's throwing well, and that the Chiefs anticipate him being a full participant at practice on Wednesday is a great sign for his availability going forward.

MORE: Harrison Butker keeps missing field goals and Chiefs fans have had enough

This was where things were trending already with Mahomes' injury, but it's still a huge piece of news for the Chiefs to hear from Reid that Mahomes is doing this well.

Facing off against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 10, Mahomes might not need to throw a whole lot, not with how good Kenneth Walker III and Emmett Johnson have been running the ball this season.

But it's still some great news to hear that Mahomes is well on his way to playing in Week 10, especially after what looked to be a major injury during the Chiefs vs. Jets game.

With Josh Downs joining the squad after a trade deadline move, Mahomes and this Chiefs offense appear to be at full strength heading into the second half of the regular season.

text:
The Detroit Lions continue to face significant injuries on both sides of the ball.

Lions coach Dan Campbell provided injury updates before practice in Allen Park on Wednesday, Nov. 11, saying that there is a "way outside shot" that center Cade Mays and cornerback D.J. Reed will play against the New England Patriots on Sunday in Munich, Germany. Reed suffered an injured hip during the Lions' Week 8 win over the Minnesota Vikings, with Mays suffering an ankle injury in the same game.

Neither played during the team's Week 9 win over the Miami Dolphins.

Though the Lions will likely be missing both players for the Germany game, Campbell provided a positive update on edge rusher D.J. Wonnum, who also left the Minnesota game with a head injury. Campbell said Wonnum "cleared his first obstacle" and will resume practicing this week.

"Once he gets some practice, [Wonnum] should be good to go," said Campbell.

Campbell also provided a small update for safety Kerby Joseph, who has already been ruled out of Sunday's game, saying there has been "no setbacks" in his recovery. He added, however, that the Lions acquired safety Andre Cisco in part because of Joseph's injury situation.

"We gotta be mindful, we may need depth here," Campbell said.

And in non-injury news, Campbell noted that left guard Christian Mahogany will be taking first-team reps in practice on Wednesday after missing last Sunday's game for violating team rules.

text:
Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid confirmed Monday that the elbow injury to quarterback Patrick Mahomes is minor and that the star signal caller is day-to-day ahead of a road matchup against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday.

Mahomes, 31, was receiving treatment at the team's practice facility Monday morning.

"It looks like it's just a matter of (getting) some rehabbing in there and getting rid of some of the soreness," Reid said Monday. "We'll just see where it goes from there. He's in good spirits."

Mahomes sustained the injury to his throwing arm late in the first half during Kansas City's 35-12 victory over the New York Jets on Sunday. He completed 23 of 31 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns but said afterward that his arm did not feel right early in the second half.

An MRI exam after the game revealed an elbow strain or sprain but no significant damage, NFL Network reported. Mahomes will be monitored for pain and swelling in the coming days.

"Anytime it's elbows and knees it's always scary because you just don't know," Mahomes said after Sunday's victory. "Even my knee (injury) last year, after we did the initial test, I could walk off the field and I thought I was going to be good. ... Once I could throw the football (Sunday) ... I knew it wasn't ligament-type stuff and it was more muscle-type stuff."

Chiefs backup quarterback Justin Fields took five snaps Sunday and lost a fumble on two rushing attempts for minus-1 yard.

text:
BEREA, Ohio (AP) — Deshaun Watson will start at quarterback for Cleveland on Sunday against Houston after missing last week's game because of a concussion and watching from the sideline as Shedeur Sanders nearly rallied the Browns to a win.

Coach Todd Monken waited until Wednesday to announce that he's sticking with Watson ahead of Sanders, who had some nice moments in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss in New Orleans.

Watson has led the Browns (5-4) to five comebacks wins season and now will face the Texans, who drafted him in 2017 before trading him to Cleveland in a blockbuster deal five years later. This will be Watson's third game against his former team.

Monken was noncommittal about his QB on Monday, saying he wanted to meet with his offensive staff before choosing his starter.

Watson sustained a concussion in the first quarter of a game against Pittsburgh on Nov. 1. He missed only one play, finished the game and didn't show any symptoms until the day after the 27-6 loss. He wasn't cleared from protocol until Saturday and Monken decided to start Sanders, who had taken all the practice snaps during the week.

Sanders, who made seven starts as a rookie last season, struggled for the first three quarters against the Saints. However, he made several positive plays in the fourth quarter and OT, finishing with 297 yards passing, two touchdowns and a 114.6 rating.

That was good enough to make Monken, who is in his first season as Cleveland's coach, consider going with him this week. But with the surprising Browns still in the playoff chase, Monken instead will go back to Watson, who is in his final year under contract.

Who would have thought that Shedeur Sanders taking over the field against the Saints would backfire on him? The Browns quarterback is now facing backlash over his postgame interview and the hype surrounding him.

"The fact that they had an interview for him after a loss is crazy," Micah Parsons said on The Edge with Micah Parsons. "I've never seen that in the NFL. Like I saw that he had a hype video out. Like when he was going to be the starter."

Quincy Avery also supported Parsons' reaction, saying, "That he did. I didn't think that was true either. Like I had to double-check that. It's awkward and it's, I don't understand like what his infatuation is."

These comments came after Shedeur Sanders gave interviews following the Browns' loss to the Saints. During the postgame press conference, he was also asked whether he had done enough to earn the starting job.

Shedeur Sanders' controversial sideline moment has even veteran defenders questioning what they witnessed. Subscribe to stay on top of the NFL's most talked about storylines.

"I think that's a setup question, honestly," Shedeur Sanders said in the postgame press conference. "I control what I control. But what I think, in the grand scheme of things, doesn't really matter. I think being a great teammate, being a great whatever role I have on the team, I could do, because you got to look at the bigger picture. We're out here connecting with each other, growing, learning in different areas. … You can't really ever look at the situation as negative."

Sanders got the opportunity to start after Deshaun Watson took a helmet-to-helmet hit during the first quarter of the Browns' game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Watson was checked for a possible concussion but was cleared to return and continued playing. However, he later developed concussion symptoms and entered the NFL's concussion protocol, which kept him out of the game against the Saints.

Sanders also created some hype around his first start of the season. On November 7, he shared a clip on Instagram featuring highlights from his NFL career, along with the caption, "Thank you GOD $²." The timing of the post, just a day before his game against the Saints, drew attention and gave the media another reason to discuss him.

However, it is not as if Sanders failed to perform against the Saints. Despite the loss, he completed 19 of 31 pass attempts for 297 yards and two touchdowns without throwing an interception. He averaged 9.6 yards per attempt, recorded a passer rating of 114.6 and a QBR of 40.2, but was sacked five times for a loss of 37 yards.

His performance also sparked a debate about who should be Cleveland's starting quarterback the following week. CBS Sports analyst Bill Cowher was among the media personalities who supported Sanders and wanted him to keep the job.

"Shedeur Sanders should be the starter for this football team. He's going to be the future, and I think what he showed today – his resilience – he continued to come back, he made great decisions, he extended plays," Cowher said during CBS Sports' postgame show. "I love the way he played, and I would move forward with Shedeur Sanders."

But despite all the hype, things might not go Sanders' way. The Cleveland Browns are planning to bring Deshaun Watson back as their starting quarterback for their Week 10 game against the Houston Texans. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported this on Monday, November 9, citing a source.

This comes even after Sanders played well against the Saints. However, head coach Todd Monken did not confirm who would start when reporters asked him about the decision on Monday.

"I really haven't thought through it other than getting through this morning's tape," Monken said. "We just got done meeting with the guys; they'll flush the game, and then we'll have a chance to meet offensively more extensively a little bit later today."

Now, let's wait and see who gets the starting quarterback role in Week 10.

title: Breaking Down the Wide-Ranging Impact of Zach Sieler's Injury on the Dolphins Defense
description:
How It Impacts the Dolphins Pass Rush Sieler’s impact on Miami’s pass rush cannot be overstated.
Along with being their most frequent one-on-one winner on the interior, Sieler has mastered stunts and games.
Without Sieler, the cohesiveness and aggression that this group has evolved into over the last couple of weeks takes a significant hit.
How It Impacts the Dolphins Run Defense Sieler’s run-game skill set is also unique.
Down the stretch of the season, rookie Trey Moore may also have an impact stepping into that hybrid role.
text:
In the final hours before the NFL Trade Deadline, it was revealed that the Miami Dolphins would be losing defensive lineman Zach Sieler for the remainder of the season with ruptured biceps that occurred in Miami’s Week 9 matchup with the Detroit Lions.

Sieler has been the Dolphins’ most consistent defender in 2026, and for a unit that has come alive over the last month, this injury means having to adapt to life without Miami’s longest-tenured player, which will certainly be difficult given his diverse skill set.

How It Impacts the Dolphins Pass Rush

Sieler’s impact on Miami’s pass rush cannot be overstated. Along with being their most frequent one-on-one winner on the interior, Sieler has mastered stunts and games. His timing and hand placement are stellar when occupying blocks and allowing the likes of Josh Uche and Chop Robinson to get to the backfield unscathed.

Without Sieler, the cohesiveness and aggression that this group has evolved into over the last couple of weeks takes a significant hit. Utilizing his ability on pick stunts was Miami’s primary method of generating pressure, and while Uche and Robinson have certainly showcased their isolation skills, Jeff Hafley no longer has an “easy button” on crucial downs. Miami will certainly keep these looks in their gameplan, but with Sieler carrying so much of that workload prior to this injury, it’s unknown how steep the drop off in effectiveness will be.

How It Impacts the Dolphins Run Defense

Sieler’s run-game skill set is also unique. As Miami's lightest and most twitchy rotational player on the interior, he’s often tasked with shooting a gap, while Jordan Phillips and/or Kenneth Grant absorb and attempt to deconstruct blocks. His ability to quickly disrupt while maintaining strong positioning often leads to runs being bounced away from him and where other defenders can rally and tackle.

Replicating this is where I think head coach Jeff Hafley can be creative. Rather than simply using Phillips or Grant, both of whom have worked better clogging lanes and occupying double teams, it wouldn’t be shocking to see one of Miami’s edges see more work slanting to the inside, while Jordyn Brooks or Willie Gay Jr., who are at their best against physicality, play a strong-side linebacker role as de facto edge defenders on run downs. Gay already occupies a similar space when on the field, and moving him to a more run-first role may eliminate some of the struggles he has in pass coverage.

Down the stretch of the season, rookie Trey Moore may also have an impact stepping into that hybrid role. Moore has spent the entirety of the 2026 season on injured reserve with an ankle injury, but appeared to be a starter prior to going down.

Next Man Up

Potentially the biggest impact of losing Sieler isn't schematic, but rather what he provides as a leader among one of the youngest positions in the league. Sieler, a team captain who has been with Miami since 2019, has been a part of three different regimes, and had adopted the role of mentor to Kenneth Grant, Jordan Phillips and Zeek Biggers, all of whom were selected in the 2025 draft.

Now, the pressure is on Miami’s three young interior pieces to not only fill in the gap Sieler left, but also prove that they’re foundational pieces of a rebuild under a different coach than the one that drafted them. With the aforementioned Grant returning from injury in Week 5, the puzzle pieces appeared to be falling into place over the last month, but now this unproven unit must operate without its key cog.

Miami’s defense, which had prioritized simply getting to a point where everyone could play their 1/11th effectively, now needs its youngest group to pick up extra slack, and the question of whether they can could be one of the early turning points of the Jeff Hafley era.

text:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- The San Francisco 49ers addressed their need at wide receiver before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, trading forIndianapolis Colts for veteran Keenan Allen.

The rebuilding Colts received a sixth-round selection in the 2027 draft in exchange for Allen.

Allen was one of two Colts wide receivers traded before the deadline, along with Josh Downs, who was traded to the Kansas City Chiefs.

It marks the second trade in three weeks between the 49ers and Colts, who also dealt star defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to San Francisco on Oct. 27.

San Francisco's need at receiver has been glaring for much of the season as injuries have ravaged that room, starting in training camp when Ricky Pearsall went on injured reserve because of knee surgery.

The Niners since have played multiple games without Mike Evans (Achilles tendonitis),Deebo Samuel Sr.(hamstring), Demarcus Robinson (ankle), De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) and Christian Kirk (calf/knee).

The trade will be a sort of homecoming for the 34-year-old Allen, who played collegiately at nearby Cal. The six-time Pro Bowler has 1,095 career receptions -- the eighth most in NFL history and seven short of surpassing Cris Carter for seventh on the all-time list.

Allen becomes the third veteran player traded in recent weeks by Indianapolis, joining Buckner and star guard Quenton Nelson.

Allen's 40 receptions were the most on the Colts this season, and he should fit right in on an offense that leans heavily on experienced veterans. According to ESPN Research, the Niners have the most offensive snaps (2,943) and offensive touchdowns (25) from players 30 or older this season.

Of the five players who are 33 or older to post 300-plus receiving yards this season, the Niners now have three of them: Allen, Evans and tight end George Kittle.

Although Robinson returned from injured reserve last week against the Las Vegas Raiders and Samuel is set to return to practice Wednesday, the 49ers have been seeking reliable options for quarterback Brock Purdy as Evans and Stribling continue to recover from their injuries.

Second-year receiver Jordan Watkins has emerged in recent weeks, including a four-catch, 86-yard, one-touchdown performance against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday.

The 49ers will need to make a corresponding move to create a roster spot for Allen. But with Samuel on track to return as soon as this week, the Niners could enter Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys with a top-four receiver corps of Robinson, Watkins, Samuel and Allen.

Coincidentally, if Allen is able to play Sunday, it will mean playing against the Cowboys two weeks in a row. He had four catches for 26 yards against Dallas in Week 9.br/]

text:
Join the huddle. Sign up here for Ravens updates in your inbox.

One month after trading for the Philadelphia Eagles’ Cam Jurgens, the Ravens added another center just before the NFL’s trade deadline Tuesday.

The Ravens sent guard Andrew Vorhees and a conditional 2028 sixth-round draft pick to Atlanta for Ryan Neuzil, who has been the Falcons’ starting center since the start of the 2025 season.

The move bolsters the Ravens’ depth at center, where they’ve lost three contributors to injury since August. It also protects the development of first-round pick Vega Ioane, who was pressed into duty at center earlier this season because of injuries up front. The team views Ioane as a a foundational piece at guard, where he starred in college.

The Ravens (4-5) have faint playoff hopes after four straight losses, but their activity over the past week, highlighted by a trade for quarterback Jacoby Brissett, underscores their intention in restoring an offense hampered by quarterback Lamar Jackson’s injuries and a revolving door along the offensive line.

“I like our team,” Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Monday. “Now, we need to play better, and we need to do things better. But we have some good players that we need to coach better. We need to get them to play the way that we’re capable of playing. If we do that, we’ll be capable of doing what we want to do.”

Starting center Cam Jurgens, another midseason trade acquisition, has held up well in pass protection since he cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol in Week 7, allowing four pressures and no sacks in three starts, according to Pro Football Focus. The 6-foot-3, 301-pound Neuzil allowed nine pressures and one sack in nine starts for the Falcons, and his run blocking skill set could give the Ravens cover if Jurgens struggles or is sidelined by injury.

Jurgens also started three games this season at left guard for Philadelphia, though he struggled and acknowledged after his trade last month that it “feels natural to be back at center.” Starting left guard John Simpson, a key free-agent signing for Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta this offseason who has played through a groin injury for most of the season, has allowed 10 pressures over the past four games.

Neuzil played guard in college but has spent all but a few NFL snaps at center. He has experience working with Ravens offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford, who coached in Atlanta before coming to Baltimore.

Neuzil, who’s in the final year of a two-year, $9.5 million deal, could bring the Ravens a late-round compensatory pick in 2028 if he signs elsewhere in the offseason.

Vorhees arrived in Baltimore three years ago as a low-risk, high-reward prospect. He’d slipped to the seventh round of the 2023 draft after tearing his ACL at the NFL scouting combine. After sitting out his rookie year, Vorhees started three games in 2024 and all 17 last season despite uneven play in pass blocking and run blocking. He struggled in the preseason in Baltimore but made the Ravens’ 53-man roster, going on to appear in five games with two starts.

Vorhees’ departure leaves the Ravens thin at guard, as 2025 third-round pick Emery Jones has been a healthy scratch in recent weeks. Ioane is coming back from a knee injury as well.

The Ravens’ deal for Neuzil was the team’s third trade since Oct. 7, making them one of the NFL’s busiest teams in a league with just 18 in-season trades total. After trading a 2028 second-round and 2027 fifth-round pick to Philadelphia for Jurgens and a 2027 seventh-rounder, the Ravens on Friday finalized a trade for Brissett. In exchange for the stopgap starter, the Ravens sent the Arizona Cardinals a 2027 fourth-round and 2028 seventh-round pick. The Ravens also received a 2027 fifth-round pick in the swap.

title: Rams' dream season has been a survival test. Now Puka Nacua is out | Opinion
description:
So far, this season of destiny for the Rams – who climbed above .500 (5-4) for the first time this season on Sunday – has become an exercise in Murphy’s Law.
“I’m bummed,” Rams coach Sean McVay told reporters at the team’s headquarters on Monday.
Then again, limping into the playoffs is no formula for a Super Bowl ticket.
It’s apparent the Super Bowl drought will continue, going on 31 years.
After a bye in Week 11, the Rams face the Packers, Chiefs and 49ers in a three-game test.
text:
If the NFL playoffs were today, guess who would be at home watching?

The Los Angeles Rams. The offseason champs. The team bookies installed as the betting favorite to play Super Bowl 61 in their own stadium – before L.A. was thrashed by the 49ers in their season opener in Australia, before all sorts of other stuff since then hit the fan.

So far, this season of destiny for the Rams – who climbed above .500 (5-4) for the first time this season on Sunday – has become an exercise in Murphy’s Law.

Whatever can go wrong, will go wrong.

And more bad news came on Monday when the team confirmed that star wideout Puka Nacua is headed to injured reserve after suffering sprained ligaments in his right knee and a turf toe. He will miss at least a month.

It figures that Nacua was injured running a jet sweep on, of all times, the final offensive play of the 20-13 victory at Washington.

“I’m bummed,” Rams coach Sean McVay told reporters at the team’s headquarters on Monday. “When these things happen, the first thing is you feel for the players. They put so much work in and it’s so unfortunate.

“Then you question, ‘What could you have done to maybe avoid it?’ ”

The Rams just can’t win for losing one way or another. After all, Nacua’s star receiving mate, Davante Adams, is already on IR, mending a ruptured hamstring. Cornerback Trent McDuffie, one of the prized offseason additions, has missed the past three games due to a back issue layered on top of a groin injury. Jaylen Watson, the other prized cornerback from the offseason haul, is done for the year because of shoulder surgery. The O-line just lost left guard Steve Avila to a hamstring injury with no definitive timeline for a return. And Myles Garrett, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year obtained from the Browns in a blockbuster trade, just came back on Sunday after missing two months following knee surgery.

The midseason checkup on McVay’s team is brutal. They have become the Bad News Rams, complete with inexplicable losses. They blew a 16-0 halftime lead at Denver in Week 3, punctuated by Matthew Stafford’s record-setting pick-six. They lost against Buffalo in Week 5 after since-released kicker Harrison Mevis’ 48-yard try for a game-winning field in overtime was blocked. Six days later, the defense didn’t give up a touchdown. But the Rams lost to Arizona, anyway, when Chad Ryland kicked his sixth field goal of the game as time expired.

They could’ve, would’ve and should’ve won all three of those games. All losses.

You can’t blame Aaron Donald, the Hall of Fame-credentialed D-tackle who came out of retirement after a two-year layoff, if he wondered: I came back for this?

Yeah, bro, it’s been rough.

For all the adversity, though, it would be foolish to write off the Rams just yet.

This is the NFL. Strange things happen.

Over the past three seasons, eight teams have made the playoffs after being .500 or worse through their first eight games. The Rams were two of those teams, rallying from a 3-5 start in 2023 and a 4-4 mark in 2024. And L.A., during the 2021 season, was also the last team to earn a Super Bowl berth without being one of the top three seeds in its conference.

Then again, limping into the playoffs is no formula for a Super Bowl ticket.

One thing for certain: the fiery McVay (whose late grandfather, John, was the personnel whiz attached to Bill Walsh as they launched the 49ers dynasty during the 1980s) will have his competitive creativity gene stretched to the hilt while trying to build on a three-game winning streak.

Nacua caught 14 passes on 19 targets for 150 yards on Sunday to raise his season totals to 70 receptions for 715 yards. And now, without Adams, the Rams must replace that production?

“We won’t have some tendencies, that’s for sure,” McVay said. “We’ll figure out what that looks like to be able to get the best different groupings and best people involved. Guys will be asked to step up.”

That’s the NFL way. It’s a war of attrition. Although the Rams’ issues are undoubtedly pronounced, every team has some level of injury-related challenges. At one extreme, the Ravens are collapsing without star quarterback Lamar Jackson. The Giants, meanwhile, are hanging tough after absorbing the “shock sandwich,” as John Harbaugh described it, of losing quarterback Jaxson Dart and linebacker Brian Burns, the team’s best defensive player. At the other end of the spectrum, the 49ers have a share of the NFL’s best record (7-1) while battling through setbacks that include the extended absence of defensive end Nick Bosa and the decimation of a receiving corps that includes Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel.

So, no, the Rams get no pity from their bitter NFC West rival.

They also have much company in the misery department when it comes to teams pegged as contenders when this season began. The defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks (5-4) wouldn’t be in the playoffs right now, either, challenged to find a way on offense to complement the greatness of Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The defending AFC champion Patriots (5-4) are three games in the loss column behind the Bills in the AFC East race. The Cowboys? It’s apparent the Super Bowl drought will continue, going on 31 years. And the NFC East drought rolls on, too.

And no, there were no quick fixes from the trade market (not for the Rams, unlike the Bears and Jaguars), even with GM Les Snead’s typically deft maneuvering with personnel moves. Shoot, even if there were, the premium draft capital to exchange has already been used.

Adjustments and growth from within will determine L.A.’s fate. Perhaps the battle-tested team, stocked with savvy vets, can get key players back from injury and jell at the right time to make a run down the stretch.

It won’t be easy. After a bye in Week 11, the Rams face the Packers, Chiefs and 49ers in a three-game test. Two of their final three games are against the Seahawks. Yes, there’s a lot of football left to close the gap and make a legit run for the postseason.

Never mind that so much was expected of this team before the season started.

“I think it’s about just improving every single day,” McVay said. “Every single game it’s let’s reset, reload, six seconds at a time.”

In the meantime, the Super Bowl vision that so many had for the Rams will be measured on a different type of clock during the second half of the season to avoid a 10-count.

text:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones denied Tuesday that the contract statuses of wide receiver George Pickens and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. played a role in either missing Sunday's win over the Indianapolis Colts.

Jones addressed the speculation during an appearance on 105.3 The Fan (h/t ESPN's Todd Archer), saying, "[It's] 100 percent injury related. Put it to rest."

Pickens missed Dallas' 27-23 road victory with shoulder and hamstring injuries, while Porter did not play due to an ankle ailment.

Per Archer, Pickens first suffered the shoulder injury against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Oct. 8, and the hamstring issue popped up over the past two weeks.

As for Porter, he has been hampered by his ankle for "the past few weeks," and left the Cowboys' 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Nov. 1 because of it.

Both Pickens and Porter are currently slated to become free agents at the conclusion of the season, which likely contributed to talk of something other than injuries playing a role in them not playing on Sunday.

The Cowboys acquired Pickens in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers prior to the 2025 season, and he went on to have a career year, earning Pro Bowl honors after recording 93 receptions for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns.

Pickens has clearly been behind CeeDee Lamb in the pecking order this season, though, resulting in more modest numbers to the tune of 39 catches for 533 yards and two touchdowns in eight games.

The Cowboys struck another deal with the Steelers this season, acquiring Porter on Sept. 30.

Porter has been hampered by injuries since the trade, though, limiting him to four games, during which he has registered eight tackles and three passes defended.

Like Pickens, the Cowboys did not sign Porter to a new contract when they acquired him, meaning he could potentially hit the open market during the offseason.

While it has been a roller-coaster season for the Cowboys thus far, they are second in the NFC East with a 4-5 record, trailing only the 5-2-1 New York Giants.

Dallas will likely need Pickens and Porter to play significant roles down the stretch in order to make a playoff run, and Jones' comments suggest that their impending free agency won't be part of the decision-making process regarding whether they play.

Buffalo Bills @ Minnesota Vikings

Bills adjust to wide receiver injuries: The Bills have dealt with wide receiver injuries all season, and now they won’t have Joshua Palmer for the rest of November with a hamstring injury.

The Bills began the year with a clear top-four wide receivers on the depth chart, with DJ Moore, Keon Coleman and Palmer as their three outside receivers and Khalil Shakir as their slot receiver. Moore has not been a full participant in practice since Week 2 due to a shoulder injury, which caused him to miss two games. Coleman appeared on the injury report for four weeks with an ankle injury, and this week, he was limited in practice with a shoulder injury. Palmer also missed time with a shoulder injury, and now it’s a hamstring injury that led him to land on injured reserve earlier today.

The Bills have two other wide receivers on the active roster in Skyler Bell and Greg Dortch. They view Dortch mostly as a special teams player. Buffalo opted to activate veteran Trent Sherfield from the practice squad and make Bell inactive, which isn’t a great sign for the rookie's future.

Buffalo spent the game with Moore and Shakir consistently playing in 11 personnel, with Coleman leading a rotation with Sherfield. In 12 personnel, all four wide receivers saw significant playing time. Coleman was the primary receiver in 13 personnel, prompting all three to see similar snap rates and route participation marks.

The injuries to the outside receivers have made Shakir more fantasy-viable. He’s played half of the 12 personnel snaps since Week 3 after rarely playing there last season. That’s led him to play over two-thirds of the offensive snaps, compared to 60% last year. He led the Bills in receiving with four receptions for 58 yards. He’s gained at least 55 yards in four of his last five games.

Minnesota adjusts without Jauan Jennings: The Vikings slot receiver was limited in practice on Thursday with a calf injury, didn't practice on Friday and Saturday and was ruled out.

When everyone is healthy, the Vikings have a straightforward wide receiver rotation with Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison playing every down and Jennings playing in 11 personnel. Unfortunately, it’s been rare that all three have been available. Jennings missed Week 2 due to personal reasons; Jefferson left Week 3 early, leading him to miss Week 4 with an ankle injury; and Addison was out for Week 5 with a hamstring injury. The Vikings had their bye, and then had two weeks at full strength.

Whenever one of the Vikings’ outside receivers was inactive, Tai Felton took over, and when Jennings was out in Week 2, it was Myles Price who replaced him. It was reasonable to expect the same for this game, with one wrinkle. The Vikings signed wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. from their own practice squad on Monday. Beckham began the season as a backup for the New York Giants, and this was his first game on the Vikings' roster after spending a few weeks on the practice squad.

Price was the third wide receiver for Minnesota, with Felton and Beckham only playing a few snaps each. It would be difficult for a third wide receiver in this offense to have fantasy value even if they were playing well, and it’s impossible with how the Vikings played in this game.

Miscellaneous Notes

Minnesota quarterback Kyler Murray didn't practice all week with a hamstring injury and was ruled out on Saturday. Carson Wentz took over as the starting quarterback, while Max Brosmer was active as the backup.

The Vikings signed running back DeeJay Dallas from their own practice squad on Wednesday. He had either been on the active roster or was a practice squad call-up most of the season to be their passing-down back. Minnesota continued its three-man backfield at running back, making it difficult to trust any of the three backs for fantasy purposes.

Minnesota running back Demond Claiborne was limited in practice on Thursday with a knee injury and didn't practice on Friday and Saturday. The Vikings placed him on injured reserve on Monday.

Buffalo wide receiver Tyrell Shavers was a full participant all week with a knee injury and was questionable, but remains on the physically unable to perform list.

Defense Notes

Buffalo cornerback Dee Alford returned after missing two of the last three games with an ankle injury. He was back to his usual role as the slot cornerback in nickel and dime defense. Anthony Kendall held the slot role in Week 5, while Te’Cory Couch had it in Week 8.

Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was reinstated from suspension on Monday, and the Bills released him on Tuesday. Gardner-Johnson had been a full-time starter before spitting at a Raiders player, leading to his suspension. Damar Hamlin has taken over as the starting safety next to Cole Bishop, and appears set to hold that role over the rest of the season. The Bills activated safety Geno Stone from the practice squad on Monday to be their third safety in dime looks for a second straight week.

The Vikings made first-round rookie defensive lineman Caleb Banks a healthy inactive for this game. He played 107 snaps as their fifth interior defender over the first eight weeks, but he held a 30.5 overall defensive grade. 2025 undrafted rookie Elijah Williams took his spot after Williams was a healthy inactive the last seven weeks.

Defensive tackle Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins left in the middle of the third quarter with an ankle injury and didn’t return. If that injury ends up being serious, it’s possible Banks will be active again next week.

Vikings safety Theo Jackson was inactive due to a quad injury. Minnesota has used Josh Metellus as its main safety, with Jackson rotating with Harrison Smith at the other safety spot. Jackson had played more in run situations and Smith more on passes. Undrafted rookie Jacob Thomas took Jackson’s spot as the early-down safety in the first half, but after a few poor plays, Smith ended up being more of a full-time safety in the second half.

Bills cornerback Christian Benford (wrist), safety Damar Hamlin (cramping), and Vikings linebacker Blake Cashman (unknown) were all reported or spotted with injuries, but all were able to return to play briefly after their respective absences.

text:
The Detroit Lions won't have All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph on the field when they travel to Munich, Germany, for a game against the New England Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 15.

Lions coach Dan Campbell confirmed during his weekly radio hit on Costa & Jansen with Heather on 97.1 The Ticket that Joseph, who returned to practice on Oct. 28 for the first time all season, still isn't ready to take the field in an actual game.

"I don't see him playing in Germany," Campbell said.

Wednesday, Nov. 11, will mark two weeks since the Lions opened Joseph's 21-day acclimation window as he hopes to return from the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list. He missed all of training camp with a lingering knee injury that dates back to before the 2025 season. He hasn't played since Week 6 of the 2025 season.

After returning from Munich, the Lions will have until next week to decide whether to add Joseph to the 53-man roster or shut him down for the season. The earliest he will return to the field is on Nov. 22, in a game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field.

Joseph, 25, was named a First-Team All-Pro in his last healthy season after netting a league-high nine interceptions in 2024. He was rewarded with a four-year, $86 million contract extension, making him the highest-paid safety in NFL history at the time.

Joseph took it slow in his first week at practice, participating only in group and individual drills before adding full-team work to his plate last week.

Lions safeties coach and assistant head coach Jim O'Neil said on Friday, Nov. 6, that Joseph looks even better than he expected.

"Yesterday was his first team practice," O'Neil said, "and he looked a lot better than what I anticipated him looking (like). So it was very encouraging."

O'Neil was hesitant to discuss any further plans for Joseph, since the nature of the injury could, in theory, involve setbacks. But the team has been pleased with how he's looked so far.

So even if he won't be on the field when Detroit tries to slow down quarterback Drake Maye and the Patriots' passing attack, it still seems promising that he'll be back in uniform sooner rather than later.

text:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- Dolphins defensive tackle Zach Sieler will miss the remainder of the season because of a ruptured biceps, leaving Miami without a critical team leader and captain.

Sieler suffered the injury on the first play of Sunday's loss to the Detroit Lions, the source told Schefter, and he still played 49 snaps on defense and special teams. He is expected to fully recover from the injury in five to six months.

Sieler was drafted by the Baltimore Ravens in the seventh round of the 2018 draft and was claimed off waivers by the Dolphins the following season. He established himself as a productive starter in Miami, registering consecutive seasons with 10 sacks in 2023 and 2024.

Sieler signed multiple extensions with the Dolphins, most recently a three-year, $64 million deal in 2025. His extension did not stop the Dolphins from drafting three defensive tackles in 2025, including first-round pick Kenneth Grant, fourth-round pick Jordan Phillips and seventh-round pick Zeek Biggers -- each of whom play regularly on Miami's defensive line.

Sieler embraced his role as the leader in the room, even on a rebuilding team, and said their additions haven't changed his desire to spend the remainder of his career in Miami. Sieler recorded two sacks this season, both against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 4.

With Sieler injured, the second-year trio of Grant, Phillips and Biggers will see an uptick in snaps. Sieler's injury also puts to bed any rumor that he will be traded before Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET deadline.

With the Dolphins sitting at 1-7, Sieler had been one of few veteran players who could attract attention from contenders in need of defensive line help. He told reporters last month that he wasn't thinking about any potential trade and wanted to win with the Dolphins. Coach Jeff Hafley also told reporters that Sieler is a valuable leader whom he loves having on the team.

"I've kind of said it over and over again - I love Zach. I love him as a person. I love him as a player," Hafley said. "I love talking to him on and off the field and the enthusiasm he brings, the leadership he brings. I can't say enough good things about the guy and how much I appreciate and how much I respect him. So that's how I feel about him."

text:
The Miami Dolphins announced Tuesday that they are placing quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve.

Willis has had a lingering groin injury that has been impacting his mobility. The quarterback had an MRI, and it showed that it is now a core muscle injury. Willis doesn't need surgery, but the amount of rest required to recover necessitated an IR stint.

With Willis sidelined for at least the next month, backup quarterback Kyle McCord is expected to take over as the starter this weekend against the Indianapolis Colts, per ESPN's Adam Schefter. Willis is not expected to miss the remainder of the season.

Willis joined the Dolphins this offseason, signing a 3-year, $67.5 million deal in free agency. He reunited with new Miami head coach Jeff Hafley, who was with Willis last year in Green Bay as the defensive coordinator.

Willis has played in eight games this season and has thrown for 1,396 yards, 6 touchdowns and 6 interceptions.

The 27-year-old is known for being able to use his legs and has picked up 232 yards and three additional scores on the ground. Willis is currently Miami's second-leading rusher behind Ollie Gordon (463 yards, 4 TDs).

McCord was a sixth-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft by the Philadelphia Eagles. He spent the season on Philadelphia's practice squad, but joined the Packers in the offseason on a reserve/futures contract.

The quarterback was then traded to the Dolphins in late August for a 2028 sixth-round pick to replace Quinn Ewers, whom Miami traded to the Jacksonville Jaguars.

McCord has yet to play a snap in his pro career, but that is expected to change Sunday against the Colts, as he is in line to make his first career start.

Brady Cook is currently Miami's only other quarterback, and he is on the practice squad.

The Chicago Bears escaped with a 27-24 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on "Sunday Night Football," but it came at a steep price.

Second-year wide receiver Luther Burden III left the game late in the fourth quarter with a concussion after taking a helmet-to-helmet hit from Buccaneers rookie edge-rusher Rueben Bain Jr.

No flag was thrown on the play. However, Bears fans want a lot more than a flag after seeing Burden lay on the field after the vicious hit.

Bears Fans Want Rueben Bain Suspended

The debate over whether Bain's hit was dirty or just bad timing hasn't slowed down. Fans are divided over whether or not it was just incidental contact.

However, there were plenty of Bears fans calling for the NFL to suspend Bain for the hit.

"Absolutely gross they let Bain get away with that hit. Dude has no idea how to tackle at all, he needs to be suspended before he seriously injures someone else. He's going to turn out to be Vontaze Burfict 2.0," one fan exclaimed.

"Just tell us when that Rueben Bain suspension drops and the league admits a flag should have been thrown. The NFL quietly stopped flagging this stuff it's disgusting," another fan replied.

Others demanded the NFL punish Bain in the form of a fine for what happened.

"Rueben Bain Jr. lowered his head and launched into Luther Burden, who was knocked out before he hit the ground. If the NFL actually cares about player safety, this gets reviewed and fined. @NFL @NFLFootballOps," one fan stated.

"@NFL make sure Ruben Bain Jr get's a hefty fine for being a dirty f— player. All of @Buccaneers defenders either go for the knees or go helmet to helmet," another fan scoffed.

"This replay clearly shows Bain trying to hit with his shoulder and Burden lowering his head. I hope he's ok but Burden is the one who makes this a dangerous play and will probably get fined for it," one user noted.

"Bain is gonna get fined at least $20k for that tomorrow," another user added.

Rueben Bain's Hit on Luther Burden Went Unflagged

The incident happened on a short pass on third-and-7 from the Bears' 15-yard line with four minutes left in the game. Burden tried to fight his way to the sticks, but the 270-pound Bain led with his shoulder and drilled him square in the helmet.

Burden crumpled face-first to the turf and fumbled. Buccaneers safety Ifeatu Melifonwu recovered, and Tampa Bay tied the game two plays later.

Burden was helped off the field and taken to the blue medical tent, and he didn't return. Head coach Ben Johnson confirmed the diagnosis after the game.

Not everyone agrees the hit was dirty. Some argued Bain was simply going for a legitimate tackle, leading with his shoulder, and that the helmet contact was incidental.

A suspension still seems like a long shot for a play that didn't draw a flag. But Bain isn't completely off the hook. The NFL reviews game film every week and typically announces fines on Saturday, so a fine could be coming even without a penalty on the field.

The good news for Chicago is that the bye week comes at the perfect time. Burden will have two weeks to clear the concussion protocol before the Bears host the New Orleans Saints on Nov. 22.

text:
There indeed was a major announcement regarding Miami Dolphins defensive tackle Zach Sieler on the day of the NFL trade deadline, but it had nothing to do with him being moved.

Instead, the bombshell report involved a season-ending injury for the team captain.

Sieler ruptured a biceps tendon against the Detroit Lions on Sunday and will undergo season-ending surgery, according to ESPN insider Adam Schefter, citing sources.

The longest-tenured member of the roster, Sieler had been remarkably durable since joining the Dolphins as a waiver pick-up from the Baltimore Ravens in 2019, missing only two games over the past six seasons — that came in the 2024 season when he was poked in the eye during practice.

STRANGE SERIES OF EVENTS

To say this news came out of nowhere would be putting it mildly, considering Sieler played 42 snaps in the 19-9 loss against the Lions, only four fewer than he played against New England in Week 8.

There also was no Sieler injury reported in the press box, with the only one reported by the Dolphins being the quad injury to Will Kacmarek after he took a shot after catching a pass near the sideline.

No injury being reported could be explained by Sieler not being tended to on the field or being away from the sideline at any point.

What is notable, however, is that on the very first play from scrimmage against Detroit, a 2-yard run by Jahmyr Gibbs, Sieler was sporting a black contraption around his right upper arm. Sieler was listed on the injury report last week with a shoulder injury and was a limited participant in practice Wednesday and Thursday before being full go Friday.

Against the Lions, Sieler finished with one tackle, good for a 3-yard loss on a running play by Gibbs. While he didn't register a stat on the play, it was his initial pressure on Jared Goff that forced the quarterback out of the pocket and led to the third-down sack by Josh Uche in the first half.

SIELER STAYING PUT

The injury obviously quashed any notion of Sieler being traded before the 4 p.m. ET deadline Tuesday, even though reports indicated earlier the Dolphins had no intention of moving on from him regardless.

Sieler has three more years left on the contract extension he signed in September 2025. He's got a cap number of $20.8 million next year with no guaranteed salary remaining, which would seem to make him a potential candidate for a contract restructure.

That's down the line, though.

The immediate impact is the Dolphins will be left without their best defensive lineman.

Veteran wide receiver Tyreek Hill is hopeful of being medically cleared to play within a few weeks.

His agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said Tuesday on The Pat McAfee Show that he still has hopes on signing somewhere during the 2026 NFL season.

Once the trade deadline passes, Hill could potentially be an option for teams that need to bolster the passing game.

The eight-time Pro Bowler is a major wild card, though, given the severity of the knee injury that has kept him out for more than a year. So much of his success was owed to his speed and acceleration out wide, and he may not possess that same explosion anymore.

Not to mention, we're already halfway through the season.

During an earlier appearance on The Pat McAfee Show, Rosenhaus said Hill's doctors suggested a comeback might have to wait until October. It's now mid-November and the veteran wideout may be another few weeks away.

The Kansas City Chiefs have been a popular choice for Hill given his previous experience with the team and the injuries to the Chiefs' receiver room. Tyquan Thornton could be sidelined for the remainder of the year, while both Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy have picked up minor knocks.

Maybe a reunion is something Kansas City will consider.

text:
Receiver Brandon Aiyuk has been reinstated to the San Francisco 49ers by the NFL after leaving the team a year ago.

The league removed Aiyuk from the reserve/left squad list on Monday and gave the 49ers a two-week exemption before they need to add him to the 53-man roster.

Aiyuk had submitted his request for reinstatement after hiring Drew Rosenhaus as his agent. He met with the 49ers last Friday as part of his attempt to get back into the NFL.

Aiyuk has not played for more than two years since injuring his knee in October 2024 but said last week that he's healthy and wants to return to the league.

The Niners have said they have no plans to play Aiyuk again and could either trade him before Tuesday's deadline or release him before the two-game exemption expires.

The 49ers are also seeking to get money back from Aiyuk. A person with knowledge of the situation said the league sent Aiyuk and the NFL Players Association a letter last week saying that he owes the 49ers about $13 million based on bonuses he was paid after signing a four-year, $120 million extension just before the start of the 2024 season. The person spoke on condition of anonymity because the letter was not released.

Aiyuk had been on the reserve/left squad list since leaving the Niners late last season.

He fired agent Ryan Williams during his long-running dispute with the 49ers and was without representation until he recently hired Rosenhaus.

The 49ers previously voided $27 million guaranteed in Aiyuk’s contract for 2026 for failing to participate in meetings and other team activities last summer when he was rehabilitating his knee injury.

Aiyuk signed the big extension just before the start of the 2024 season following a lengthy contract hold-in that kept him out of training camp. He was coming off a 2023 season when he had 75 catches for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns and was a second-team All-Pro.

Aiyuk had only 25 catches for 374 yards in seven games in 2024 before getting injured. The 28-year-old has 294 catches for 4,305 yards and 25 TDs since being drafted in the first round in 2020.
